chapter: Southern Illinois roadhouse and St. Louis
title: Berger's job terms and paying off Doc Moon
summary: Berger offered thirty-odd dollars a week plus room, whiskey-making and car-stealing, and Doc Moon furiously accepted his ninety dollars.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, so you'll get back to...

Yeah, so to get back to Charlie... I says, 'Well, what about the money?' He says, 'I'll pay you [what was it?] thirty dollars a week or thirty-five...' -- I can't remember exactly. He says, 'But, I'll give you a place to stay, and we make whiskey here and beer in the daytime, and if you want to work doing that, or if you want to run some liquor, you can make some extra money; if you want to steal some cars...'
That was his very words. Because that's what they did.
Well, that was a good-paying proposition if you did what he said.

I says, 'Okay, I'll do it. But you have to give me some money to pay Doc Moon for that saxophone.' And in that day, you were supposed to give a two... There wasn't a union, but it was an unwritten law that you had to give a two-week notice on many of these shows. So when I went to give Doc Moon his ninety dollars, he almost had a
He didn't want you to leave.
The first thing he said, 'I'm gonna tell your Dad when I get back to Baton Rouge what you did to me!' Anyway, I gave him his ninety dollars, and I started working with Charlie and them.
